cues.text: 大家好，欢迎收听我的中文
速成学习播客。 如果你是
第一次来到我的频道，我是一名
汉语作为第二语言的教师
，上个月我
在越南做了一名数字游民。 在今天的
视频中，我想和大家分享我
在越南的生活经历。 你可能会问我为什么
选择越南。 主要原因
其实很简单：我看到一些
我喜欢的英语博主
在那里生活和创作内容。 我
想在这里解释一下“
游牧生活”这个概念——它与
旅游截然不同。 旅游通常
持续时间较短，但游牧生活
意味着你会在一个地方停留更
长时间，与当地人一起生活并融入其中
。 例如，
这次我在越南待了一个月。 我
突然很想做这件事，于是
告诉了一个朋友，他们说：“别
犹豫了，去做吧！” 不要
等到下个月或下周；
现在就去做。 我也认为，当你
真心想做某件事的时候，就不
应该想太多。 如果你想得
太多，就会
因为害怕未知而轻易找到借口，
然后你就不会去做。 有时
恐惧的声音会占据上风，阻止我们
去做事。 所以，第二天
我就申请了越南签证。
越南对中国公民并非免签
，但您只需
在线填写一些简单的信息，然后等待
大约三到四个工作日即可。 我
记得签证费是25美元。
第二个原因是
生活成本相当低； 越南的住宿、
餐饮和交通
比许多其他国家都便宜。
出发前，我估算了
在越南一个月的生活费用，
包括机票、签证、住房、食物
和交通，大约是10000
元人民币，不到1500美元。 之前
我在云南待了一个月，花费
了7000元人民币，约合1000美元。 我觉得
只要游牧生活的成本在
我的预算之内，那就
完全不是问题。 我之前提到过“
生活成本”这个词； 它指的是
在某个地方生活所需的费用
。 最后我留给你们
两个问题：第一，你们国家
每月的生活成本大约是多少
？ 你认为哪个国家的
生活成本最高？
抵达越南后，给
我留下最深刻印象的
是摩托车的数量之多。
有时我站在
没有红绿灯的十字路口，等了好
几分钟都没找到合适的
过马路机会，所以在越南过马路真的需要自信
和勇气
。 与我在马来西亚的生活相比
，我觉得越南的道路要
好得多，因为在马来西亚，
道路基本上是为汽车而建的，而不是
为行人而建的。 至少在
越南，到处都有人行道
，而且交通信号灯也更多
。 因为
摩托车很多，所以司机们都习惯了按喇叭
。 我在越南住过四间不同的 Airbnb 民宿
，虽然它们
都有隔音玻璃门，但我每天还是
不可避免地会听到摩托车的噪音
，不过我似乎已经逐渐
习惯了。
融入当地生活方式的一种方法是乘坐
摩托车出租车。 在我的记忆中，它们
在我小时候就存在，但现在
它们正在逐渐消失。
那时候，发生过一些可怕的新闻，比如有
女孩吸毒后被杀之类的
。 如今在中国，
你偶尔还能看到一些
非官方的摩托车出租车； 所谓
非官方，是指他们不
通过网约车平台。 我
认为现在没多少人会选择
使用它们。 在越南，由于
街道总是非常拥挤，乘坐
摩托车出租车比乘坐
普通出租车更快，而且更便宜
，价格可能只有普通出租车的三分之一或近一半
。 所以，我
在越南经常会乘坐摩托车出租车
。 有时候我会
遇到开得很快的司机
，坐在后座上我会非常紧张
。 如果时间已晚或者我
要去比较偏远的地区，我会
选择乘坐普通出租车而
不是摩托车出租车。 在这一部分，我
提到了一些感想，所以最后我留给
大家两个问题。 第一个问题
是，你如何看待第一
印象？ 为什么？ 第二个问题
是，在你过去的旅行中，什么事件给
你留下了深刻的印象？ 在中国
，很多年轻人喜欢去
咖啡馆工作，
越南也是如此。 然而，越南
咖啡有其独特的
特点，例如鸡蛋咖啡。
我第一次听说的时候觉得很奇怪
——鸡蛋和咖啡怎么能结合在一起呢？    这
鸡蛋难道不会有很重的鱼腥味吗？
后来，我去试了一下。 我抿了一口，
发现味道非常香醇
浓郁； 你甚至尝不出一丝
蛋腥味。 还有椰子
咖啡，它配有一小杯
浓缩咖啡和一大杯
椰奶； 你可以自己把浓缩咖啡倒入
椰奶中。
天气炎热时，喝一杯冰凉爽口的
椰子咖啡真是令人神清气爽。
最后，我最喜欢的是越南
海盐咖啡。 它既有
咖啡的甜味，又有
海盐的咸味。 我
平时不怎么喝
咖啡，但在越南，我
几乎每天都喝咖啡，因为越南
咖啡实在太好喝了。
我在越南首都河内经历了一件非常神奇的事情
。 我
走进一家越南河粉店，
墙上的菜单全是越南语。 我
试着用英语请年轻的服务员
帮我挑选一道特色
菜。 但他听不懂我的
英语，所以我拿出手机使用
翻译器。 当他看到
我屏幕上的中文界面时，他就开始用
中文和我说话。 我
心想，我从未想过中文会
超越英语成为全球通用语言。
越南语和汉语一样，也有
声调，有些词的发音也
相当相似。 所以，我认为
越南人学习中文可能相对容易一些。
你的母语有声调吗？
你的母语里有没有
和汉语发音相似的词？
因为我的工作是线上办公，所以我只需要一台
电脑。 旅行让我可以
在一个地方长时间停留，并有
机会深入体验
当地的生活方式。 到达一个
新的地方后，我们才意识到
世界上有很多不同的生活方式。 这些经历帮助我成为一名
更好的中文老师
。 它们让我更好地
了解它们的文化，使我成为一个
更具包容性的全球公民，并帮助
我成为更好的自己。    在
越南的这段时间里，我不仅
欣赏到了许多美丽的风景，也
面临了许多挑战。 我感觉自己
比以前勇敢多了，因为我相信
无论遇到什么困难
，我都有能力解决它们。
面对诸多事情时，恐惧有时会
占据我们的大脑，替我们发声。
所以，当事情发生时，我会问
自己，我是选择勇敢还是恐惧。 如果
答案不是恐惧，那么我就可以
更好地面对控制，并放下
恐惧。 好了，今天的
分享就到这里。 如果你也去过
越南，请在评论区告诉我
你最喜欢
越南的哪个地方。 如果你还没去过
越南，你最想在
那里体验什么？ 如果你喜欢这个
慢节奏的中文播客，请点
赞并订阅。
下个视频见！

en_cues.text: Hello everyone, welcome to my Chinese
speed-learning podcast. If this is your
first time on my channel, I’m a
teacher of Chinese as a second language
, and I spent last month living as a
digital nomad in Vietnam. In today’s
video, I want to share my experience
living in Vietnam. You might ask why I
chose Vietnam. The main reason is
actually quite simple: I saw some
English-speaking vloggers I like living
there while creating content. I’d
like to explain the term "living as a
nomad" here—it's quite different from
tourism. Tourism is usually for a
shorter duration, but living as a nomad
means you stay in one place for a
longer time, living and blending in
with the locals. For example, I stayed
in Vietnam for a month this time. I
suddenly felt the urge to do this, so I
told a friend, and they said, "Don't
hesitate, just go for it!" Don't wait
for next month or next week; do it
right now. I also think that when you
truly want to do something, you
shouldn't overthink it. If you think
too much, you'll easily find excuses
because of the fear of the unknown, and
then you won't do it. Sometimes the
voice of fear takes over and stops us
from doing things. So, the very next
day, I applied for a visa to Vietnam.
Vietnam is not visa-free for Chinese
citizens, but you only need to fill out
some simple information online and wait
about three to four business days. I
remember the visa fee was $ 25. The
second reason is that the cost of
living is quite low; accommodation,
food, and transportation in Vietnam are
cheaper than in many other countries.
Before I left, I estimated the cost of
living in Vietnam for a month,
including flights, visa, housing, food,
and transport, which is about 10,000
RMB, or less than $ 1,500. Previously,
I spent a month in Yunnan, and the cost
was 7,000 RMB, or about $ 1,000. I feel
that as long as the cost of living as a
nomad is within my budget, it’s not a
problem at all. I mentioned the term "
cost of living" earlier; it refers to
the expenses required to live in a
certain place. I’ll leave you with
two questions: first, what is the
approximate monthly cost of living in
your country? Which country do you
think has the highest cost of living?
After arriving in Vietnam, the thing
that left the deepest impression on me
was the sheer number of motorcycles.
Sometimes I stood at an intersection
without traffic lights, waiting for
minutes without finding a good chance
to cross, so you really need confidence
and courage to cross the street in
Vietnam. Compared to my life in
Malaysia, I feel the roads in Vietnam
are much better, because in Malaysia,
the roads are basically for cars, not
for people to walk on. At least in
Vietnam, there are sidewalks everywhere
, and there are more traffic lights as
well. Because there are so many
motorbikes, drivers are used to honking
. I've stayed in four different Airbnbs
in Vietnam, and even though they all
have soundproof glass doors, I still
inevitably hear the noise of motorbikes
every day, though I seem to be getting
a bit more used to it. One way to blend
into the local lifestyle is by taking
motorbike taxis. In my memory, they
existed when I was a child, but now
they are gradually disappearing. Back
then, there was some scary news, like a
girl taking one and getting killed or
something like that. In China today,
you can occasionally see some
unofficial motorbike taxis; by
unofficial, I mean they don't go
through a ride-hailing platform. I
don't think many people would choose to
use them now. In Vietnam, because the
streets are always so congested, taking
a motorbike taxi is faster than taking
a regular taxi, and it’s much cheaper
, probably about a third or nearly half
the price. So, I actually find myself
taking motorbike taxis quite often in
Vietnam. There are times when I
encounter a driver who goes really fast
, and I get really nervous sitting on
the back. If it's late at night or I'm
heading to a more remote area, I will
choose to take a regular taxi instead
of a motorbike taxi. In this section, I
mentioned impressions, so I’ll leave
you with two questions. The first one
is, what do you think about first
impressions? Why? The second question
is, in your past travels, what incident
left a deep impression on you? In China
, many young people like to go to
coffee shops to work, and it’s the
same in Vietnam. However, Vietnamese
coffee has its own unique
characteristics, like egg coffee. When
I first heard of it, I found it strange
—how can egg and coffee be combined?
Wouldn't the egg taste very fishy?
Later, I went to try it. I took a sip
and found the flavor was very fragrant
and rich; you couldn't even taste a
hint of egg. Then there is coconut
coffee, which comes with a small cup of
espresso and a large cup of coconut
milk; you can pour the espresso into
the coconut milk yourself. When the
weather is hot, drinking a cool, icy
coconut coffee is truly refreshing.
Finally, the one I prefer is Vietnamese
sea salt coffee. It has both the
sweetness of the coffee and the
saltiness of the sea salt. I’m not
someone who has a habit of drinking
coffee, but in Vietnam, I drink it
basically every day because Vietnamese
coffee is just that delicious.
Something amazing happened to me in
Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam. I walked
into a pho restaurant where the menu on
the wall was entirely in Vietnamese. I
tried asking the young waiter in
English to help me choose a specialty
dish. But he didn't understand my
English, so I took out my phone to use
a translator. When he saw the Chinese
interface on my screen, he started
speaking Chinese to me. I thought to
myself, I never expected Chinese to
surpass English as a global language.
Vietnamese, like Chinese, also has
tones, and the pronunciation of some
words is quite similar. So, I think it
might be relatively easier for
Vietnamese people to learn Chinese.
Does your native language have tones?
Are there any words in your native
language that sound similar to Chinese?
Because I work online, all I need is my
computer. Traveling allows me to stay
in one place for a long time and gives
me the chance to deeply experience the
local lifestyle. After arriving in a
new place, we realize that there are
many different ways of living in the
world. These experiences help me become
a better Chinese teacher for my
students. They allow me to better
understand their cultures, make me a
more inclusive global citizen, and help
me become a better version of myself.
During this time in Vietnam, I not only
saw many beautiful sights but also
faced many challenges. I feel much
braver than before because I trust that
no matter what difficulties I encounter
, I have the ability to solve them.
When facing many things, fear sometimes
occupies our brain and speaks for us.
So, when something happens, I ask
myself if I choose courage or fear. If
the answer is not fear, then I can
better face control and let go of my
fear. Alright, that's it for today's
sharing. If you have also been to
Vietnam, please let me know in the
comments what your favorite place in
Vietnam is. If you haven't been to
Vietnam yet, what would you most like
to experience there? If you like this
slow Chinese podcast, please hit the
like button and subscribe. See you in
the next video!
